title: Private VPC control-plane outage: postmortem and action items after upgrade + DNS regression
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a scheduled control-plane patch rollout to private/VPC customers on 2026-03-10 we observed a severe outage for a subset of customers. Symptoms included persistent API timeouts to the private control plane, failing host registration, and self-healing jobs stuck in retry loops. Root cause traces point to an interaction between the new control-plane agent behavior and our DNS cache invalidation policy which allowed stale DNS records to persist after the control-plane VIP moved during the rollout. The end result: prolonged control-plane disconnects for ~4.2 hours for affected tenants and degraded autoscaling/health reconciliation for up to 7 hours as edge caches expired.
timeline: 2026-03-10 01:00 UTC - Scheduled rolling upgrade window opened for private control-plane agents (canary first)
2026-03-10 01:12 UTC - Canary agent reported successful restart and health, rollout continued to 10% hosts
2026-03-10 01:45 UTC - Pager alert: multiple private tenants reporting control-plane timeouts; automatic rollback did not trigger
2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Engineering triage: control-plane VIP moved to new host; many tenants continued to use old VIP IP due to long DNS TTL and intermediate cache behavior
2026-03-10 02:30 UTC - Immediate mitigation: increase agent DNS refresh frequency and push configuration toggle to refresh caches; support enabled temporary TCP proxy fallback for critical tenants
2026-03-10 05:20 UTC - All affected tenants regained stable control-plane connectivity after cache expiry and targeted cache flush operations
2026-03-10 06:00 UTC - Post-incident meeting: decided on action items and new pre-upgrade gating checks
root_cause: Two simultaneous shortcomings combined: (1) a control-plane agent change that performed implicit VIP migration without a synchronized announcement channel, and (2) an overly permissive DNS caching policy in our on-prem/private agent and edge proxies which allowed stale A records to persist across the migration. The control-plane change increased the probability of VIP movement during rollout; caches and DNS resolvers retained the old IP for longer than anticipated, preventing kube-like heartbeats and RPCs from reaching the new control-plane endpoint.
mitigation: Immediate: toggled DNS refresh on agents and flushed edge caches for impacted customers; enabled TCP proxy fallbacks for critical customers
Near-term: reverted the canary roll where we could and paused remaining rollouts while we validated cache behavior and announced plan to customers
Long-term: implement coordinated VIP cutover with explicit announcement channel, reduce hard DNS TTL for control-plane records for private customers, add automatic cache-invalidation hooks on rollout
action_items: AP-1: Implement an explicit control-plane announcement/coordination channel (gossip or signed endpoint bundle) to avoid implicit VIP moves during upgrades; owner: Priya Khatri; due: 2026-03-20; status: in progress
AP-2: Add DNS TTL policy and enforcement for private/VPC control-plane records: default TTL=30s and configurable per-region; owner: Marcelo Ortiz; due: 2026-03-18; status: assigned
AP-3: Build agent-side aggressive cache invalidation toggle + safe default to refresh DNS on rollout; owner: Linh Tran; due: 2026-03-15; status: in progress
AP-4: Create e2e upgrade simulation harness that includes real-world DNS resolver behavior and cache layers; owner: SRE Team (ENG-4773); due: 2026-04-01; status: planned

AP-5: Update rollout runbook to include a preflight check for outstanding DNS caches and to coordinate cache flush with customers if needed; owner: On-call Runbooks Squad; due: 2026-03-14; status: in progress
AP-6: Instrument control-plane VIP migration events in telemetry and add alert if >0.5% of agents report mismatched DNS/IP for >2m; owner: Observability (ENG-4882); due: 2026-03-22; status: planned
AP-7: Postmortem communication: send targeted follow-up to impacted customers with RCA and remediation timeline; owner: Customer Success (R. Patel); due: 2026-03-12; status: completed
